name: castle portcullis gate set in the wall
label: beodeul_dungeon/earth.portcullis

surfaces.part: portcullis grate with iron bars and cross bands, set flat in the wall opening
stone wall surround with a lighter coping row at the top

answer.evidence: The object is a flat wall-mounted portcullis drawn face-on. Iron bars run vertically between horizontal cross bands at rows 10 and 17, inside a dark frame with a rounded top. The stone wall surrounds it, with a light coping strip at row 0. There is no top surface, no ellipse and no roof or eave shadow, and no side face is visible. Rows 0-3 are a flat wall course, not a horizontal surface. This is a flat wall-mounted piece, so a front elevation is expected for this kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate carries 13 visible tones per 16x16 tile. That is above the hedge (9) and close to the cheese stall (17) and roofed well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%. Only 21% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans toward a tinted dark stone tone rather than a uniform black sticker line. The stone wall has individually shaded blocks with light top edges and darker joints, in about 4 steps. That is slightly fewer than the references' 5-6, but it is not a flat body with one shade and an outline. The arch interior is dark, with iron bars in two or three tones. Total colours are low (15), but the hedge reference is similarly economical (11) and reads as rich. The piece sits acceptably next to the references and does not look thinner or flatter. The bars are somewhat uniform, which is the main weakness.
